heroHeadline: Senate Reconciliation Week of May 18 Approaches with Byrd Rule Battles Ongoing; NPR Finds Trump Enforcement Surge Cuts Undocumented Worker Participation 4–5% with U.S. Worker Spillover
heroSubtitle: NPR Planet Money published research on May 12, 2026 documenting a measurable economic chilling effect from the Trump immigration enforcement surge: undocumented worker participation has fallen an estimated 4–5%, with spillover harm to U.S.-born low-education workers competing in the same labor markets, and cascading effects in agriculture, construction, and hospitality supply chains. Senate committees are preparing for May 19 markups on the $71.7 billion immigration enforcement reconciliation bill — ICE would receive approximately $38.2 billion, roughly 8× its FY2024 base budget — ahead of a full Senate floor vote the week of May 18 and Trump's June 1 signing deadline. Senate Republicans were actively weighing whether to strip the controversial $1 billion White House ballroom security provision to avoid a Byrd rule parliamentarian ruling that could jeopardize the bill. The American Immigration Council published a 14-point enforcement reform blueprint on May 12 calling for replaced mass deportation with a tiered accountability system — including restored OIDO oversight, minimum detention medical care standards, and reinstated prosecutorial discretion — published one week before the markups of a bill that contains none of these protections. Active ICE Director Todd Lyons' May 31 resignation looms with no named successor. The 287(g) program has reached 1,797 active MOAs across 39 states, and FY2026 deaths in custody stand at 30+ — a record pace — with the Office of Immigration Detention Ombudsman shuttered since May 5.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, court records, and Congressional records
